items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had heard some records of Duke with a growl trombone player named Tricky Sam.

ctx.x: Connie's Inn and the Cotton Club were in the heart of Harlem but the only negroes that went there were the ones that worked there. These two cabarets catered for the wealthy clientele that called going to Harlem, slumming. Both clubs had extravagant floor shows and the artists were the best in the business as were the orchestras.

I don't remember what orchestra was playing at Connie's at the time but I think it was a semi-classical one. At the Cotton Club which was 2 blocks from the Savoy going in the direction of 145th Street an orchestra called Duke Ellington was playing and I heard that Freddie Jenkins was in the band. I had heard some records of Duke with a growl trumpeter named Bubber Miley and a growl trombone player named Tricky Sam.

Next door to the Cotton Club was the Lenox Club which was for negro but white people were also admitted. The leader of the band was Banjo Bernie and there was a breakfast dance every Monday. It started at 5 o'clock in the morning and most of the club musicians and entertainers would meet there to enjoy being together after a week of going to work in the places they were engaged. I started going there when I first heard about the breakfast dance when we were at the Capitol. The thing lasted until the last party…
